discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: In 2013 IceCube reported the first evidence of a flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, later confirmed at high significance. This opened a new window on the universe: neutrinos travel unaffected by magnetic fields and matter, so they point straight back to the most energetic cosmic accelerators. The observations were followed by the association of a neutrino with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017) and the Galactic-plane neutrino emission (2023). Francis Halzen conceived the idea of turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a particle detector. As principal investigator he drove it through AMANDA to IceCube, a detector that was technically very hard to build. The idea is simple and the realisation was extraordinary. The discovery is clearly defined and marks the birth of high-energy neutrino astronomy, a new branch of multi-messenger astrophysics.
